Data.subject: Resident Households
Data.title: Resident Households By Age Group Of Household Reference Person And Household Living Arrangement, Annual
Data.footnote: Data for 2000, 2010 and 2020 are based on the Census of Population while data for 2005, 2015 and 2025 are based on the General Household Survey.  Data for all other years are based on the Comprehensive June Labour Force Survey.  Survey estimates are subject to sampling variability.  Data on Household Living Arrangement have been revised in Jun 2026 to be based on the composition of members within the household, instead of the characteristics of the household reference person to provide a more holistic view of household living arrangements.

row.footnote: Married couple-based with children refers to households with at least one married couple living with their child(ren), regardless of age.
Married couple-based without children refers to households with at least one married couple and none are living with their child(ren).  This includes couples with child(ren) who have moved out.

Lone-parent refers to households with no married couple and at least one never-married/ widowed/ divorced/ separated person who is living with his/ her child(ren).  The child(ren) must be aged below 16 years or are never-married to be considered.
One-person refers to one-person households.  Examples include single persons living alone, or ever-married persons who are living alone as their child(ren) have moved out.

All other households that do not fall under any of the above household living arrangement categories.  Examples include: 1) A divorced person living with his/her widowed parent.  2) Elderly living only with domestic worker.  3) Only siblings living together without parents.  4) Friends living together.
